the coupling between agent internal and agent/environmental dynamics is an essential ingredient in the development of simple and robust spatial representation in evolving robots.

a) the robot/environmental coupling can be used to generate a spatial representation of the environment, and b) that the robot/environmental and robot/robot couplings can generate a temporal representation of the robot's internal state.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of how a population of simple agents can autonomously develop the ability to self-locate and to distinguish different locations in their environment, and to generalize their skill to new situations.

a fundamental problem of artificial intelligence: How can autonomous agents develop forms of spatial representations in order to discriminate different locations in their environment and to self-localize?
the study of how a population of autonomous agents can self-organize and develop a form of internal spatial representations which allow them to exploit the spatial structure of their environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evolved robots have come up with a simple and robust solution that is able to solve the self-localization problem in a wide variety of environments, and that this solution is based on the exploitation of the quasi-periodic limit cycles emerging from the coupling of a robot's environmental and internal dynamics.

the evolved robots develop a form of spatial representation by exploiting a dynamical coupling between their internal and environmental dynamics, and this allows them to develop a form of self-localization that does not require any external reference frame.
the robots are able to develop a form of spatial representation by exploiting a simple form of temporal coding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robots autonomously develop forms for spatial representation which are based on a form of temporal coding.

we have demonstrated how an agent can develop spatial representations by exploiting its internal dynamics, and by integrating sensory-motors information over time, without the need of any explicit spatial or geometric representation.

the evolved robots are able to develop forms of spatial representations that are based on the temporal dynamics of the internal states of the robots and that allow the robots to self-localize in the environment by using a simple form of temporal integration of the sensory information.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coupling between agent internal dynamics and agent/environmental dynamics can be a powerful source of self-organization, which allows agents to develop forms of spatial representations without the need of any explicit spatial information.
the coupling between agent/environmental and agent/ internal dynamics can be a powerful mechanism to develop spatial representations and self-localization skills in autonomous agents.

the coupling between internal and environmental dynamics can be exploited by evolving robots to develop forms of spatial representations that allow them to self-organize in a complex environment and to discriminate different environmental locations.
